extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark dataset for REmote Sensing Image Scene Classification (RESISC), created by Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU). This dataset contains 31,500 images, covering 45 scene classes with 700 images in each class.
extraction.creator: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, Xiaoqiang Lu
extraction.citeAs: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, and Xiaoqiang Lu, Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art, Proceedings of the IEEE, 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was extracted from Google Earth (Google Inc.) by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation. Images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Google Earth (Google Inc.) satellite imagery, aerial photography and geographic information system (GIS) 3D globe.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were extracted with a size of 256x256 pixels in the red green blue (RGB) color space.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation extracted and categorized images into 45 scene classes. The scene classes were selected by investigating existing datasets and searching keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: High within-class diversity and between-class similarity makes the dataset challenging. Some scene classes are quite similar in vision (e.g., church and palace, dense residential and medium residential), which increases the difficulty in discriminating the scene images.
